title: Effectiveness of Curriculum Learning Depends on Reward Sparsity and Competing Optima
abstract: arXiv:2610.31884v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: While animals and people tend to learn a task more quickly and reliably when they first train on simpler versions of it, curriculum learning's effectiveness in artificial settings varies, and appears substantially greater in reinforcement learning than in supervised learning. In this work, we construct and analyze a minimal model of policy learning to better understand why. We consider an open-loop, episodic target interception task whose parameters---especially how close the agent must be to the target to receive an informative reward signal---can be chosen so that the agent either receives informative rewards frequently ('dense' rewards) or rarely ('sparse' rewards). We mathematically and numerically analyze the dynamics of REINFORCE-based policy learning in both cases. In the dense reward case, curricula have only marginal benefits; in the sparse case, curricula can be required for learning to occur at all. We find that this is espe

translated_title: 课程学习的有效性取决于奖励稀疏性与竞争最优解
translated_abstract: 尽管动物和人类在先训练较简单版本的任务时，往往能更快、更可靠地学会该任务，但课程学习在人工环境中的有效性却各不相同，且其在强化学习中的效果似乎显著大于监督学习。在这项工作中，我们构建并分析了一个策略学习的最小化模型，以更好地理解其中的原因。我们考虑一个开环、回合制的目标拦截任务，其参数——尤其是智能体必须距离目标多近才能获得有信息量的奖励信号——可以被设定为使智能体频繁获得有信息量的奖励（“稠密”奖励）或很少获得（“稀疏”奖励）。我们对两种情况下基于REINFORCE的策略学习动力学进行了数学和数值分析。在稠密奖励的情况下，课程只能带来边际收益；而在稀疏奖励的情况下，课程可能是学习得以发生的必要条件。我们发现，这一现象（原文摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 通过构建并分析策略学习的最小化模型，该研究证明了课程学习的有效性取决于奖励的稀疏程度：在稠密奖励下课程仅有边际收益，而在稀疏奖励下课程可能是学习得以发生的必要条件。
en_tdlr: By constructing and analyzing a minimal model of policy learning, this study shows that the effectiveness of curriculum learning depends on reward sparsity: curricula offer only marginal benefits with dense rewards but may be necessary for learning to occur at all with sparse rewards.
